originalGroup.material:
Lana's art bag

Lana has a yellow bag. She takes it to art club on Friday. There are two pencils, a small box of crayons and a bottle of water in the bag. Her paint is in the classroom.

Today Lana draws a green tree and three red birds. Her friend Sam draws a blue boat. They put their pictures on the wall.

After art club, Lana cannot find her water bottle. Sam looks under the table. The bottle is there, next to a chair. Lana thanks him and puts it back in her bag. They go home together.

originalGroup.material:
The sports bag

Mum: Hello, Alex. Are you at school?
Alex: Yes, Mum. I'm in the classroom. I can't find my sports bag.
Mum: What colour is it?
Alex: It's black, with a white star. My trainers and a blue T-shirt are inside.
Mum: Is it in your bedroom?
Alex: I don't think so. I put it beside the front door this morning.
Mum: Let me look. Oh, yes! It's here, behind Dad's coat.
Alex: Can you bring it to school? Our match starts at half past three.
Mum: I can get there at three. Where shall we meet?
Alex: At the small gate beside the library, please. The main gate is closed this afternoon.
Mum: All right. Do you need your water bottle too?
Alex: No, thanks. It's in my school bag.
Mum: See you at three.
Alex: Thanks, Mum!

originalGroup.material:
Fox and the empty envelope

In a village of talking animals, Fox made beautiful cards. One morning, Rabbit ordered a birthday card for her sister. 'Please put it in an envelope,' she said. 'I'll collect it after lunch.'

Fox made a card with silver stars. He put an envelope beside it, then went outside to help a neighbour. While he was away, a breeze blew through the window. The card slipped under a pile of paper, but the envelope stayed on the desk.

When Rabbit arrived, Fox handed her the envelope without looking inside. She opened it at home and found nothing. Instead of getting angry, she returned and asked Fox to help her look.

They found the card together. Fox was sorry. 'The envelope looked ready,' he said.

Rabbit smiled. 'A lovely envelope is useful, but the message matters too.'

After that, Fox checked every card before closing its envelope. He still decorated the outside carefully. He simply made sure that the part people could not see was ready as well.

originalGroup.material:
Science club: choose a Saturday project

The science club offers four projects this Saturday. Each student may join only one. Book by Thursday and meet in Room 6 ten minutes before your project starts. All materials are included in the price.

Project | Time | Age | Price | What you will do
Paper Bridges | 9:00-10:30 | 10-12 | 4 pounds | Build a bridge and test how many small blocks it can hold.
Birdwatch Notebook | 9:30-11:00 | 11-13 | 3 pounds | Observe birds in the school garden and make a simple record.
Moving Pictures | 11:00-12:00 | 10-13 | 5 pounds | Make a short animation using drawings and a school tablet.
Kitchen Colours | 13:00-14:30 | 12-13 | 4 pounds | Use ordinary foods to investigate changes in colour.

Birdwatch Notebook takes place outdoors. If it rains heavily, students will use photographs in Room 6 instead. The other three projects are indoors. Students in Kitchen Colours must tell the teacher about any food allergies when booking. You will not eat the materials.

You may take your bridge, notebook or drawings home. School tablets must stay in the classroom. Parents can collect students at the main entrance after each project.

The science club offers four projects this Saturday. Each student may join only one. Book by Thursday and meet in Room 6 ten minutes before your project starts. All materials are included in the price.

Project | Time | Age | Price | What you will do
Paper Bridges | 9:00-10:30 | 10-12 | 4 pounds | Build a bridge and test how many small blocks it can hold.
Birdwatch Notebook | 9:30-11:00 | 11-13 | 3 pounds | Observe birds in the school garden and make a simple record.
Moving Pictures | 11:00-12:00 | 10-13 | 5 pounds | Make a short animation using drawings and a school tablet.
Kitchen Colours | 13:00-14:30 | 12-13 | 4 pounds | Use ordinary foods to investigate changes in colour.

Birdwatch Notebook takes place outdoors. If it rains heavily, students will use photographs in Room 6 instead. The other three projects are indoors. Students in Kitchen Colours must tell the teacher about any food allergies when booking. You will not eat the materials.

You may take your bridge, notebook or drawings home. School tablets must stay in the classroom. Parents can collect students at the main entrance after each project.
questions.explanation: Moving Pictures costs five pounds. Three is Birdwatch's price and four belongs to Paper Bridges and Kitchen Colours.
questions.hint: Use the complete material and the question together.
